subsystems.name: Collector units
subsystems.role: thin, lightweight satellites that intercept sunlight and convert it to electricity or heat.

subsystems.name: Orbit and collision management
subsystems.role: keeps millions of units in stable, non-intersecting orbits close to the star.
parts: ion thrusters or solar sails for station-keeping

subsystems.name: Power beaming and reception
subsystems.role: transmits collected energy to a destination such as a planet or a receiver station.
parts: rectenna or photovoltaic receiver at the destination

subsystems.name: In-space manufacturing and resource extraction
subsystems.role: builds new collector units from asteroidal or lunar material, allowing the swarm to grow.
parts: smelters and refiners for metals and silicon

subsystems.name: Swarm control and communication
subsystems.role: coordinates the units, routes power, and manages the swarm as a whole.
parts: sensors for position, temperature, and power output

subsystems.name: Energy conversion and storage (at destination)
subsystems.role: turns the received beam into usable grid power or computation.

buildSteps.title: Survey and select feedstock
buildSteps.detail: Robotic probes map near-Earth asteroids and the lunar surface for silicon, metals, and volatiles needed to make collector units.

buildSteps.title: Establish off-world mining and refining
buildSteps.detail: Automated machines extract ore and process it into pure silicon, aluminium, and other materials without returning to Earth.

buildSteps.title: Build a prototype collector
buildSteps.detail: A single thin-film solar collector is assembled in orbit and tested for power generation, beaming, and station-keeping.

buildSteps.title: Deploy and test a small cluster
buildSteps.detail: A few dozen units are placed in close solar orbit, verifying that they can hold formation and beam power to a receiver.

buildSteps.title: Scale via self-replication
buildSteps.detail: Automated factories use mined material to build copies of themselves and of collector units, growing the population exponentially.

buildSteps.title: Expand to a partial swarm
buildSteps.detail: Millions of units form a ring or shell that intercepts a growing fraction of the star's radiant output.

buildSteps.title: Build power transmission infrastructure
buildSteps.detail: Large phased arrays or laser transmitters beam energy to a planet, moon, or other destination where rectennas convert it to electricity.

buildSteps.title: Maintain and evolve
buildSteps.detail: Failed units are recycled or replaced, and the swarm gradually expands until it captures a substantial fraction of the star's total output.

prerequisites.tech: Space-based solar power and power beaming
prerequisites.why: small-scale experiments have beamed power to Earth, but not at the scale or efficiency a swarm needs.

prerequisites.tech: Asteroid mining and in-space resource utilisation
prerequisites.why: sample returns and small experiments exist, but mining and refining at industrial scale has not been done.
robots assemble structures on the ISS, but building millions of units requires far more autonomy.
reusable rockets are reducing cost, but launching swarm components from Earth would be impractical; most material must come from space.
collectors close to the Sun face intense heat and radiation that no existing thin-film material can survive for long.

pathway.milestone: space-based solar power experiments and asteroid sample returns
pathway.unlocks: basic understanding of power beaming and off-Earth materials.

pathway.milestone: robotic mining and manufacturing on the Moon or near-Earth asteroids
pathway.unlocks: ability to build large structures from non-Earth materials.

pathway.milestone: first solar collector arrays in orbit beaming power to a lunar base or Earth
pathway.unlocks: commercial space power and experience with large orbiting structures.

pathway.milestone: self-replicating factories produce collector units exponentially, forming a partial Dyson swarm
pathway.unlocks: capture of a substantial fraction of a star's output, approaching a Kardashev Type II civilisation.
